Aoh pipeline:



- basically need to compare each monthly migrant group compared to  to the monthly ecoregional trait space (other migrants + reaidents) (and maybe to the annual trait space)- i.e. do they contribute unique functions for that month, but also are they unique annually for that ecoregion - even more profound for ecosystem functioning as their potentially keystone function is only represented in one month- then look at what this function is- savitraits (monthly). Maybe start with ellipse centroids or average nearest neighbour of each group (disprity)

Or can do sum of kernel contributions for each species in the migrant/trabsience  group (including residents I.s. Migrant/transience = 0) vs the seasonal, annual and monthly trait space for that ecoregion. E.g. if monthly migrants tend to be more unique than migrants with more months present  and they occupy unique area in the annual test space, not just the monthly or seasonal trait space may be quite profound as keystone. 


Traitspace: I will use AVONET 9 traits only x main niche in avoniche (foraging + diet simultaneously derived from a score of 60% for that niche relative to the other 32 niches, if no niche reaches this = generalist; can also get major 9 diet types, refined from Wilman et al., 2014; better for characterising how resources can be used in multiple ways by interacting with different substrates for example (Saysol et al., 2026)) with gawdis (Williams and Curley, 2025; Oliveira et al., 2023). categorical traits are weighted by Wi = 1/N i.e. niche = weights/32 (number of forgaging niche category). Include foraging traits and diet types as highly linked to ecosystem services provisioning and vertical niche partitioning between guilds.

Then is the idea to compare: 


migrants defined globally with range maps

1. migrants vs residents in annual trait space x ecoregion- are they unique in annual trait space

2. migrants vs residents  in monthly trait space x ecoregion- are they unique in seasonal trait space (Summer vs Winter vs Passage months (call passage instead of NA).

3. migrants vs residents in monthly trait space x ecoregion- are they unique in monthly trait space


migrants defined by graded scale of transience:


1. migrants present in 1 month, migrants present in 2 months, migrants present in 3 months etc until I get to residents vs  monthly trait space - are transient migrants more unique  than non-transient migrants/what is their overlap in monthly trait space- can plot on the same trait space. 

2. migrants present in 1 month, migrants present in 2 months, migrants present in 3 months etc until I get to residents vs  seasonal trait space - are transient migrants more unique  than non-transient  migrants/what is their overlap in seasonal trait space- can plot on the same trait space.

3. migrants present in 1 month, migrants present in 2 months, migrants present in 3 months etc until I get to residents vs  annual trait space - are transient migrants more unique  than non-transient 
migrants/what is their overlap in annual trait space- can plot on the same trait space. i.e. finally to identify keystone species.

4. maybe, even will go down to weekly/daily as defining migratory status gradient (for that would need species level contribution).

Then, if the results differ in terms of uniqueness between annual and monthly means either that niche switching might matter or that species are unique in terms of the month/season but not the year, maybe consider a niche switching analysis because that could reveal hidden non-uniqueness/redundnacy?


looking like will need: 

- a metric of spread i.e. sum of variances
- a metric of overlap i.e. beta diversity between two groups (beta.temp; also good for overlap between two seasonal (e.g. Almeida et al., 2023) and functional.beta.pair of the ‘betapart’ package - BUT not convex hull, controlling for nestedness and turnover (Oliveria et al., 2023)
- a metric of dispersion (positional difference) i.e. distance between centroids
- kernel.contribution, good as uses nearest neigbour distance so captures what species does to the - - clustering of trait space in some sense and less sensitive to outliers.
